protocol.question: Does a fixed random/greedy collection mixture improve fresh behavior with constrained DDQN unchanged?

conditions.label: Eight random plus eight fixed greedy episodes

collection.guided_action_selection: all4 lowest-label greedy; no mask, epsilon or oracle
collection.collector: constrained_bootstrap bank1 seed0 update30000, fixed by index

optimizer.loss: mean over states of mean SmoothL1 beta1 over each state's distinct recorded actions

sampling.baseline_reconstruction: full30000 draws checked only against archived control
sampling.target_access: own-arm recorded outcomes and successor logged masks only

evaluation.action_selection: all4 fresh greedy and epsilon0.1; no logged masks at deployment

recorded_actions.deduplication: state/action repeats must agree on reward, terminated, truncated and successor; no frequency weighting

collector_recordings.archived_control_rendering: from saved rows only, without additional world.step or predictions

limitations: Fixed8random+8greedy episodes per map changes interactions, states, actions, route availability and replay distribution together.
Guidance comes from one pretrained bank1/seed0 constrained model with prior100878 interactions/30000updates; this is extra overlapping historical knowledge.
Eight greedy slots duplicate one route per map and guided routes are shared across banks; duplicates add no loss weight.
Actual action-target and neural-query counts differ; only learner updates and sampled-state presentations are matched.
Frozen-policy collection followed by offline learning is not continuous online adaptation or memory; no new competence gate or significance claim.
